transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

I came in because, well, my head just doesn’t really stay on task anymore. It's been pretty frustrating. Like, I’ll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for this supervisor certification, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk into the supply closet and completely forget what I even went in there for. I just can't seem to focus on anything.
Did you have the same kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't remember having any issues like this when I was a kid. School was fine back then, and I could get my work done without spacing out like I do now. So, no, it wasn't really a problem when I was younger.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, actually. My sleep has been messed up for a long time now. I work overnight shifts, and a lot of times when I get home, I'll just lie in bed... like, I'm completely tired but somehow wired at the same time. And even when I do manage to get a decent number of hours of sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
Did these sleep problems start after you began working overnight shifts?

Yeah, pretty much. It's been going on for about three years now. That's when the contractor changed our schedules. They put us on these rotating evening and overnight shifts, mostly covering the larger properties, and my sleep just hasn't been the same since.
On days when you do not work overnight, do you sleep normally?

I'm not really sure anymore. I mean, because my schedule rotates so much, my body is just kind of confused all the time. So even on my days off, I wouldn't really say I sleep normally. It's still pretty much the same.
When your work schedule switches back to daytime hours for a while, does your sleep get better?

I don't really get daytime shifts... like, at all anymore. It's pretty much strictly evenings and overnights with this contractor. So, uh, I couldn't really tell you if it would get better. I just never get a stretch of normal daytime hours to find out.
Do you use marijuana?
No, I don't. I don't use marijuana at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?

Yeah, I have. Um... most days, I just feel like there's this heavy, flat feeling following me around. It doesn't really go away. Even when I'm just pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway at work, or... or if I'm sitting with my family and just trying to act normal, it's always kind of there.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um, no, I don't think so. I still do the stuff I normally like to do... like watching a game or just hanging out. I still want to do those things, and I still get something out of them. It's just, like I said, that heavy feeling is kind of sitting there while I'm doing them. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest.
When your sleep is especially bad, does that heavy, flat feeling usually get worse?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed a connection, to be honest. It feels pretty much the same most days, whether I get a decent night's sleep or not. I haven't really paid attention to if a bad night makes it heavier... it's just kind of a constant thing.
How long have you been feeling that heavy, flat feeling most days?

It's been going on for a while now... about three years, I'd say. Yeah, it started right around the time the contractor changed our schedules. They moved us to these rotating evening and overnight shifts at some of the larger properties. It's just been kind of hanging over me ever since then.
Do you often feel hopeless?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. I mean... I don't feel like giving up or anything like that. I just keep going to work and doing what I need to do every day. It's just that constant heavy feeling I mentioned before, but I wouldn't really call it hopelessness.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?
No, not really. I don't feel anxious or jittery or anything like that. It's really just that flat, heavy feeling I was talking about. I'm not on edge, just... tired and flat, I guess.
When you get home from an overnight shift and try to sleep, do you often have trouble actually falling asleep?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty messed up for a long time now. When I get home from an overnight shift, I'll just lie there in bed... I'm exhausted, but it's like I'm tired but wired at the same time, so I can't actually drift off. And honestly, even when I do manage to get a decent number of hours of sleep, I still wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
When your work schedule shifts later into evening or overnight hours, does your sleep usually get worse?

I'm not really sure if it gets worse, to be honest. It seems like my sleep is just messed up no matter what shift I'm working. Whether I'm doing evenings, overnights, or even if I work during the day... I still have that same problem. So I haven't really noticed it being specifically worse because of the schedule, it's just kind of always a struggle.
When you have enough time set aside to sleep, do you still have trouble sleeping?

Yeah, like I was saying just a minute ago, having the time doesn't really fix it. Even if I have plenty of time set aside and actually manage to sleep a decent number of hours, I still wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. So yeah, even with enough time, it's still a struggle.
Has that heavy, flat feeling been making it harder for you to function at work or at home?

Yeah, it has. I mean, I still get the cleaning done at work, but... I'm definitely slower. And I second-guess my logs so much now that I've just stopped pushing for the supervisor track entirely. I don't really feel up to it. And outside of work, I've been skipping out on things. Like neighborhood clean-ups and family get-togethers that I used to always make time for... I just don't go to them anymore.
Have you been feeling low on energy nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel low on energy. It's more just... that flat feeling we were talking about. But physically, I don't feel like I'm running on empty or anything. I just don't really have the drive to do much, but the energy itself is fine.
When you’ve had a few days away from work, does that heavy, flat feeling get better?

Not really, no. Um... even if I have a long weekend or take a couple days off, it doesn't really change much. I still just wake up with that same flat feeling. Being away from the building doesn't seem to make it lift.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I don't feel like hurting myself or anything. It's just... I just feel flat. But no, I haven't thought about ending things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent depressed/flat mood most days for about 3 years with clear functional impairment at work and socially, and denies core alternative features such as anxiety, hopelessness, suicidality, childhood inattention, and substance use. Although chronic shift-related sleep disturbance is prominent and likely contributory, the interview did not establish the key pattern needed for shift work sleep disorder (sleep disturbance clearly tied to circadian misalignment and varying with schedule), and primary insomnia alone does not account for the sustained depressed mood and associated impairment. Given the provided candidates, depressive disorder unspecified is the best fit.

confirmed_symptoms: persistent heavy, flat feeling most days
mood symptoms present while at work and with family
decreased drive and reduced engagement despite preserved interest/pleasure
social withdrawal from neighborhood clean-ups and family get-togethers
longstanding sleep problems beginning after rotating evening/overnight shifts started
difficulty falling asleep after overnight shifts despite feeling exhausted
sleep feels nonrestorative even after a decent number of hours
sleep difficulty persists even when enough time is set aside for sleep
re-reading the same line repeatedly when studying or working
forgetting the purpose of entering the supply closet
difficulty staying on task with inventory and certification studying

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Depressed/flat mood and sleep problems were both reported as present for about 3 years, beginning around the work schedule change.
additional_requirements: Functional impairment confirmed by slower work performance, abandoning supervisor track, and reduced social participation
Childhood attention problems denied, arguing against ADHD-type lifelong inattention
